clue.text: Way to provide horse for member of county set

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to afford is to provide or supply
a shire is a heavy breed of draught horse

explanation.surface: A route by which someone supplies a mount to a member of the landed gentry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'County set' suggests the snobbish landed class; here it is simply the set of English counties, of which this is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffordshire is one of the shires of the English Midlands, so it belongs to the collection of counties.

clue.text: Adjacent seats not available at this play?

definitions.text: Adjacent seats not available at this play?

parts.words: Adjacent seats not available at this play?
parts.note: a restaurant that cannot seat diners together, also the title of a Terence Rattigan drama of 1954

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a booking complaint at a theatre or restaurant, but names Rattigan's play set in a hotel dining room.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattigan's drama is set among guests dining apart in a seaside hotel.

clue.text: Rival has top cards, including king

indicators.note: the word for top cards holds the abbreviation for king inside it

parts.note: aces are the highest cards in most games
R is for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An opponent holds the best cards, a king among them.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Acres is a character in Sheridan's comedy The Rivals, so 'Rival' is a member of that cast, not a competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Acres is a comic suitor in Sheridan's play The Rivals.

clue.text: Insect in dark is not the type that settles

parts.note: a fly is an insect
by night means during darkness

explanation.surface: A bug in the dark that never lands anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settles' suggests an insect alighting, but means paying debts: a fly-by-night ducks out before paying.
explanation.definitionFit: An unreliable person who leaves without paying debts is called by this term.

clue.text: Transport on land, or sail away with 16

indicators.note: 16 down is STARTS OFF, so each of the three words loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: Travel by land, or else set off by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is the solution STARTS OFF, used as an indicator: OR, SAIL and AWAY each lose their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carries goods and people overland on tracks.

clue.text: A female has lived in this pub

parts.note: she refers to a female
been means existed or lived, as in has been

explanation.surface: A woman once lived in this bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking den, especially in Ireland and South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an illicit drinking house, an unlicensed bar.

clue.text: Unit of measure for columns in church

parts.note: taken as written; that the letters also run on unbroken through 'in church' is a coincidence of the charade, not a hidden word

explanation.surface: A measurement for pillars inside a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: Newspaper space is sold in column inches, which is why 'columns' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper copy is measured by the column inch, a standard printing unit.

clue.text: Couches in trains

definitions.meaning: to couch is to phrase or put into words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Couches' looks like sofas, but is the verb for phrasing words.
explanation.definitionFit: To couch a thought is to word it; fast passenger services stopping rarely share the plural noun.

clue.text: Gentlemen involved with a main organization?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Gentlemen tied up with a chief body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' scrambles GENTLEMEN A MAIN into the fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Line management is the structure of supervision in a company hierarchy.

clue.text: Convoluted interplay in political policy

indicators.note: convoluted means twisted and intricate, so the letters of the next word are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Tortuous back-and-forth shaping a government's official stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convoluted' turns INTERPLAY into the answer's nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's official line is the agreed stance its members must follow.

clue.text: A pair in group of islands — or, just one

indicators.note: the letter A and the abbreviation for pair go inside the abbreviation for the islands

parts.note: CI is the Channel Islands, a group off the French coast

explanation.surface: Two places within an archipelago, or perhaps only a single island.
explanation.walkthrough: CI stands for the Channel Islands, a British Crown group near Normandy. 'Just one' defines by contrast: the answer is a single Italian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is a lone island in the Bay of Naples, one island rather than a group.

clue.text: Start off full of beans? That can be dangerous

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is taken away, as if its start were knocked off

parts.note: a lively, playful person full of beans is frisky

explanation.surface: Being overexcited at the outset can get you into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full of beans' is British slang for energetic and lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hazardous carries risk, so it is fraught with peril.

clue.text: Produce tears in a small page

parts.note: wee is a Scottish word for small

explanation.surface: Someone cries over a tiny sheet of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry is to shed drops from the eyes, a synonym.

clue.text: He's rustic, she's divine

definitions.meaning: in country dialect 'he is' becomes '...', run together as one word
the Greek goddess of youth, cupbearer to the gods

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the answer as two words of rural speech; the second names a goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural dialect renders 'he is' with be, while the Greek cupbearer of Olympus was a goddess.

clue.text: It's hard to miss this instrument of torture

parts.note: iron suggests hardness, as in iron will
a maiden is a miss, an unmarried girl

explanation.surface: This torture device is hard to overlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard to miss' reads as conspicuous, but splits into two synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: The iron maiden was a spiked cabinet once claimed to be used for torment.

clue.text: Witness provided in bad-tempered case

indicators.note: the word for provided sits inside the word for bad-tempered, which forms its case

parts.note: testy means irritable or bad-tempered
if means provided, as in on condition that

explanation.surface: Testimony given in a court case with an irritable atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' completes the container picture, the holding word wrapping round the other. 'Witness' and 'case' suggest a trial, but 'case' is no courtroom matter here.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear witness is to give evidence in court, the verb sense.

clue.text: Initiates change of sort that divides the workers

indicators.note: the anagram splits the word for workers, sitting inside it

parts.note: the staff are the workers of an organisation

indicators.note: change of means the letters of sort are rearranged

explanation.surface: Begins a rearrangement of the kind that splits the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of' scrambles the four letters of sort to RTSO; 'that divides' then sets those letters inside the workforce word, splitting it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin something is to set it going, so the phrase means commences.

clue.text: She returns as temptress

indicators.note: returns means the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: a siren is a seductive woman who lures men

explanation.surface: A seductive woman comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' turns AS SIREN backwards. The answer is Portia's waiting woman in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, so 'She' fairly defines a female character.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerissa is a woman in Shakespeare, so a female pronoun stands for her.

clue.text: A head, in backward class, takes some lessons

indicators.note: the word for a head goes inside the reversed word for class
backward means the word for class is read in reverse

parts.note: a set is a class or group of pupils of similar ability
each means a head, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: A head teacher, working with a slow-learning group, conducts a few classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' turns SET into TES. 'Backward class' and 'head' paint a school, misdirecting from the price sense of 'a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor who takes classes instructs pupils, which is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Heavy weapon as part of defensive build-up

definitions.meaning: a cosh made of a sand-filled bag
sacks of sand piled to form a barricade

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a cosh, the other a sack piled into fortifications.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand-filled sack can serve as a cosh or be stacked into walls against bullets and floods.

clue.text: Players, including a bridge player, before a game of cards

indicators.note: the word for players holds the next two pieces within it

parts.note: the cast is the group of actors in a play
N is North, one of the four players at bridge

explanation.surface: Actors, with a card player among them, before a round of rummy-style cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' just sets the final A after the rest. The four bridge seats are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game played with two packs.

clue.text: One over the eight? Search for chap who's affected

parts.note: the cox steers a rowing eight, sitting over the rowers
to comb is to search thoroughly

explanation.surface: A drunk searches for a pretentious fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for being drunk; here it is the cox of a rowing crew of eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb is a vain, conceited dandy.

clue.text: Letter from Israel included in March issue

definitions.meaning: the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet
one of the March daughters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women, issue meaning offspring

explanation.walkthrough: 'March issue' reads as a magazine edition, but it means the children of the March family in Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Beth is a Hebrew alphabetic character and also one of the four sisters, Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy, in Little Women.

clue.text: Gem in ring New York Times displayed

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
x is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A jewel shown in a ring, advertised in a New York newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York Times' looks like the newspaper; it splits into NY and the times sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded semi-precious stone used in jewellery.

clue.text: Accomplished about a mile in walk

indicators.note: the word for accomplished goes about, surrounding, the abbreviation for mile

parts.note: able means skilled or accomplished

explanation.surface: A skilled hiker covered around a mile on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to stroll at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: Cheese female needed to digest

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A woman needs to eat some soft cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digest' reads as a verb about eating, but is a noun meaning summary.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief is a summary or abstract, a digest of information.

clue.text: Oriental bow, say

indicators.note: say signals the word for bow is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a bow is a knotted tie, as in bow tie

explanation.surface: An Eastern bow, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' suggests a polite greeting in Asia, but is a knot, tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Thailand is Asian, an inhabitant of the East.

clue.text: I turned to chapter to find OT character

indicators.note: turned means the word for I is reversed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone flips to a chapter to locate a figure in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' makes ONE into ENO. OT is the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Enoch is a patriarch in Genesis, father of Methuselah.

clue.text: Attack Liberal Party

parts.note: broad means liberal or tolerant, as in broad-minded
a side is a party in a dispute or contest

explanation.surface: A political party of liberals goes on the offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal Party' looks like the British political party, but splits into two synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a fierce verbal onslaught, from a warship firing all guns on one flank.

clue.text: As an added advantage, skirt has been altered to match

parts.note: to skirt is to border or edge, as a fringe does

indicators.note: altered means the letters of the word are changed in order

parts.note: to fit is to suit or match

explanation.surface: A dress hem lengthened to suit as a bonus extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered' turns BEEN into BENE. 'Skirt' and 'altered' suggest dressmaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A perk is an extra benefit on top of salary, such as a company car.
